does: Burns the skin of a whole vegetable black over an open flame or a fierce heat, so that the flesh inside turns soft, smoky and sweet, and the charred skin can be peeled away.
how: Set the whole vegetable directly on a gas flame, on a hot grill or on a barbecue.
Turn it now and then with tongs, until the skin is blackened and blistered all over and the flesh has gone soft and collapsed.
Move it to a bowl and cover it, so that the steam loosens the skin.
When it is cool enough to handle, peel off the skin and lift out the stem and seeds. Do not rinse it, or the smoky taste is lost.
Drain off the juices, or keep them for the dish, as it asks.

cues.text: The skin is blackened and blistered all over, and the vegetable has sagged.
The flesh gives completely when pressed with the tongs.

mistakes.mistake: Taking it off while the skin is only blistered in patches, so that the flesh stays firm and the skin clings.
mistakes.fix: Keep turning it until the skin is black all over and the vegetable has collapsed.

mistakes.mistake: Rinsing the vegetable under the tap to remove the skin, which washes away the smoke.
mistakes.fix: Wipe or pull the skin off by hand.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving it uncovered, so that the skin sticks.
mistakes.fix: Cover it while it steams and cools.

variant_of.differs: The whole, unpeeled vegetable sits straight on the flame and its skin is burnt black on purpose, then peeled away, so that the smoky soft flesh is what is kept.
